# Object fields

Fields set on channels, models, supplies, the allocation policy, user groups, routing policies, organizations and API keys.

## Channel

<a id="channel-priority"></a>

### Priority

Key `channel.priority` · Type int · Default 0

Where: Channels › routing

The order channels are tried in for a model: the highest priority takes requests first. A lower priority is used only while every channel above it is unavailable; channels of one priority share requests by weight. The Usage choices (only provider, backup, share, prefer) set it for you. While supplies route requests, the call order on the Providers page orders channels instead, and new supplies of the channel start from its priority.

Examples:

- `10` Tried before every channel at 0 that serves the same model in the same group.
- `0` The default. A backup at -1 is reached only while every channel at 0 fails.

See also: [Weight](./objects.md#channel-weight) · [Priority](./objects.md#supply-priority) · [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder)

<a id="channel-weight"></a>

### Weight

Key `channel.weight` · Type int · Range 0– · Default 1

Where: Channels › routing

How channels of the same priority share a model's requests: each takes its weight over the sum of the weights. Channels of other priorities are not counted. While supplies route requests, the supplies' own weights decide, and new supplies of the channel start from its weight.

Examples:

- `3` Next to a channel of weight 1 at the same priority, takes about 3 / (3 + 1) = 75% of the requests.
- `1` The default: channels of one priority share requests equally.

See also: [Priority](./objects.md#channel-priority) · [Weight](./objects.md#supply-weight) · [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault)

<a id="channel-cost_ratio"></a>

### Cost ratio

Key `channel.cost_ratio` · Type ratio · Range 0– · Default empty (unknown)

Where: Channels › advanced

What the channel's upstream charges as a multiple of the catalog price, for channels without a price list. It is used only where the channel publishes no synced price: the channel cost is then catalog price x cost ratio x (1 + fee rate). It feeds the profit figures, the supply cost and the warning on user groups sold below it; users are never charged by it. Empty or 0 means unknown.

Examples:

- `0.8` A relay at 80% of the official price: a $3 / $15 per million token model costs $2.40 / $12, or $2.52 / $12.60 with a 5% fee.
- `1` The upstream charges the official price; any group below ratio 1 is flagged as selling at a loss here.

See also: [Fee rate](./objects.md#channel-fee_rate) · [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio) · [Catalog price](./objects.md#model-price)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#where-to-set-what](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#where-to-set-what)

<a id="channel-fee_rate"></a>

### Fee rate

Key `channel.fee_rate` · Type percent · Unit % · Range 0– · Default the provider's published fee

Where: Channels › advanced

What the channel's provider charges on top of its list prices, usually when you buy credit: cash paid / credit received - 1. A channel's cost is its list price x (1 + fee rate); costs decide which supply takes a request and which ones the price check holds. Recorded top-ups set it from the latest 10.

Examples:

- `5` Requesty: $105 buys $100 of credit.
- `3` Vercel AI Gateway card payments: a $3.00 processing fee on $100 of credit.
- `0` An official vendor API billed at list price.

See also: [Payment cost](./billing.md#PaymentCostPercent) · [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder) · [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#channel-fee-rates](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#channel-fee-rates)

<a id="channel-fee_note"></a>

### Fee source

Key `channel.fee_note` · Type string

Where: Channels › advanced

Where the channel's fee rate comes from, such as a billing page or a checkout receipt. It is required once the fee rate is above 0. Only admins see it; users see a generic label.

See also: [Fee rate](./objects.md#channel-fee_rate)

<a id="channel-group"></a>

### Groups

Key `channel.group` · Type list · Default default

Where: Channels › routing

The user groups the channel serves: a request is only sent to channels of the group it runs in. A request runs in its API key's group (then the key's backup group), or the user's group when the key has none. A channel needs at least one group.

Examples:

- `default` Serves every user of the default group and keys set to it.
- `default,vip` Serves both groups; each request is billed at the ratio of the group it ran in.

See also: [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio) · [Group](./objects.md#token-group) · [Backup group](./objects.md#token-backup_group)

<a id="channel-model_mapping"></a>

### Model mapping

Key `channel.model_mapping` · Type json · rarely changed

Where: Channels › advanced

Renames on this channel only: a requested model name is sent upstream as another name. Use it only when the upstream wants its own names, such as deployment names; matching models to the catalog needs nothing here. A target starting with + bills by the requested name. Requests routed through a supply use the supply's upstream model instead. Saving a change rewrites the channel's model list to the requested names.

Examples:

- `{"gpt-4o": "my-gpt4o-deployment"}` Requests for gpt-4o reach the upstream as my-gpt4o-deployment.
- `{"opus-latest": "+claude-opus-4-1"}` opus-latest is sent as claude-opus-4-1 and billed as opus-latest.

See also: [Upstream model](./objects.md#supply-upstream_model)

<a id="channel-pre_cost"></a>

### Pre-billing

Key `channel.pre_cost` · Type enum · Default 1 · rarely changed

Where: Channels › advanced

How the gateway counts a request's input before sending it, to hold the user's credit until the reply's usage is known. The count also stands in for the input when an upstream reports no usage, such as some streams. Leaving images or everything out saves server work on heavy requests; the prompt token limit is still checked.

Values:

- `1` Normal billing: Count the input tokens, images included, before the request is sent.
- `2` Exclude images: Count the text only; images are left out of the estimate.
- `3` Exclude all: Count nothing beforehand; the reply's usage decides the charge.

See also: [Max prompt tokens](./gateway.md#MaxPromptTokens)

<a id="channel-disabled_stream"></a>

### Models with streaming disabled

Key `channel.disabled_stream` · Type list · rarely changed

Where: Channels › advanced

Models this channel must not stream: streaming requests for them skip it for another channel serving the model. Requests without streaming still use it. Empty means every model streams.

Examples:

- `o1,o1-pro` Streaming requests for o1 and o1-pro go to other channels; plain requests still come here.

<a id="channel-prompt_caching"></a>

### Prompt caching injection

Key `channel.prompt_caching` · Type enum · Default inherit · rarely changed

Where: Channels › advanced

Whether the gateway adds cache_control marks to Claude requests on this channel, so the upstream caches the prompt. Shown for Anthropic, Claude Code and OpenRouter channels, in the plugin settings. Requests that already carry cache_control are left alone. The plugin also sets the cache lifetime (5 minutes or 1 hour), where the marks go and which models match (Claude names by default).

Values:

- `inherit` Follow the site: Inject when the site-wide Claude prompt caching switch is on.
- `on` Always on: Inject on this channel whatever the site switch says.
- `off` Always off: Never inject on this channel.

See also: [Add prompt cache markers](./gateway.md#ClaudePromptCachingEnabled)

<a id="channel-proxy"></a>

### Proxy

Key `channel.proxy` · Type url

Where: Channels › connection

A proxy for this channel's upstream requests only, http or socks5. Only needed when this server cannot reach the upstream directly. A %s in the address is replaced with a session ID derived from the key, for proxies that pin one exit per session. Empty connects directly.

Examples:

- `http://127.0.0.1:1080` Every request of the channel goes through the local HTTP proxy.
- `socks5://user-%s:pass@proxy.example.com:1080` Each key gets its own proxy session, so its exit address stays the same.

<a id="channel-test_model"></a>

### Test model

Key `channel.test_model` · Type string

Where: Channels › monitor

The model connection tests and scheduled checks send their request with. Empty picks a cheap chat model from the channel's list, else its first chat model; a channel without a chat model then cannot be tested.

Examples:

- `gpt-4o-mini` Tests cost a fraction of a cent and do not touch the expensive models.

## Model

<a id="model-price"></a>

### Catalog price

Key `model.price` · Type float · Unit USD / 1M tokens · Range 0–

Where: Models › Pricing

What the model costs before the group ratio, per million input and output tokens (or per request or minute). Users pay catalog price x their group ratio, whichever channel serves the request. It can be typed in USD, RMB or as a ratio (1 = $2 per million tokens). A model without a price is refused by default.

Examples:

- `3 / 15` $3 input and $15 output per million tokens; the default group at 1.12 pays $3.36 / $16.80.
- `ratio 1.5 / 7.5` The same price as ratios: 1.5 x $2 = $3 and 7.5 x $2 = $15 per million tokens.

See also: [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio) · [Cost ratio](./objects.md#channel-cost_ratio) · [Payment cost](./billing.md#PaymentCostPercent)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#the-three-numbers](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#the-three-numbers)

<a id="model-supply_mode"></a>

### Supply mode

Key `model.supply_mode` · Type enum · Default default

Where: Models › supplies

How the supplies of one tier share this model's requests. Tiers are always tried in order; the mode only decides within one. It applies to models whose order is set by hand: a model that follows the call order always shares a tier by weight.

Values:

- `default` Follow default: Use the default supply mode of the platform settings.
- `balance` Balance: Supplies of one tier share requests by weight.
- `failover` Failover: The heaviest supply of a tier takes every request; the others back it up.

Examples:

- `failover` Supplies of weights 3 and 1 in one tier: the weight 3 supply takes every request while it works.
- `balance` The same supplies take about 75% and 25% of the requests.

See also: [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault) · [Supply order](./objects.md#model-allocation) · [Weight](./objects.md#supply-weight)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request)

<a id="model-allocation"></a>

### Supply order

Key `model.allocation` · Type enum · Default policy

Where: Models › supplies

Whether the model's supplies follow the call order of the Providers page or keep their own numbers. Changing a supply's priority or weight on the Supplies tab sets the model to set by hand; switching back to the call order drops those numbers.

Values:

- `policy` Call order: The supplies' priority and weight come from the call order on the Providers page.
- `manual` Set by hand: The supplies keep the priority and weight stored on them.

Examples:

- `policy` Moving a provider up on the Providers page moves it up for this model too.
- `manual` This model keeps its order when the call order changes; new channels join below its supplies.

See also: [Call order](./objects.md#allocation-tiers) · [Priority](./objects.md#supply-priority) · [Supply mode](./objects.md#model-supply_mode)

## Supply

<a id="supply-priority"></a>

### Priority

Key `supply.priority` · Type int · Default the channel's priority; a supply added by hand joins below the lowest tier

Where: Models › supplies

This supply's tier among the model's supplies: higher tiers take requests first, lower ones back them up. A lower tier is used only while every supply above it is unavailable. Supplies of one priority form a tier and share it by the supply mode. Under the call order the policy sets it; a supply with its own number no longer follows its channel.

Examples:

- `2` Above two supplies at 1: they are used only while this supply fails.
- `1` Next to another supply at 1, the two form one tier and share its requests.

See also: [Weight](./objects.md#supply-weight) · [Supply order](./objects.md#model-allocation) · [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request)

<a id="supply-weight"></a>

### Weight

Key `supply.weight` · Type int · Range 0– · Default the channel's weight

Where: Models › supplies

This supply's share of its tier: its weight over the tier's total under balance, all of it if heaviest under failover. 0 counts as 1. Under the call order a provider's weight is split equally between its channels.

Examples:

- `3` With a weight 1 supply in its tier: about 75% of the requests under balance, all of them under failover.
- `1` Two supplies of weight 1 share a tier 50 / 50 under balance.

See also: [Priority](./objects.md#supply-priority) · [Supply mode](./objects.md#model-supply_mode) · [Default supply mode](./gateway.md#SupplyModeDefault)

<a id="supply-enabled"></a>

### Use this supply

Key `supply.enabled` · Type bool · Default on; off for a supply an intake rule adds for review

Where: Models › supplies

Whether the supply takes the model's requests. Off, it keeps its settings but is skipped. Supplies an intake rule added wait switched off until you switch them on; switching a supply on also accepts its cost, so the price check leaves it alone.

See also: [Intake rules for new upstream models](./gateway.md#SupplyIntakeRules)

<a id="supply-upstream_model"></a>

### Upstream model

Key `supply.upstream_model` · Type string · Default filled in from the channel's mapping, its model list or its platform's naming

Where: Models › supplies

The model name this supply sends to its channel's upstream. The client still asks for the public name and is billed by it; the channel's model mapping does not apply. A supply stops taking requests when the upstream stops listing this name in two checks in a row.

Examples:

- `claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929` A Vertex channel serves the public claude-sonnet-4-5 under its own versioned name.
- `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` An aggregator that prefixes the vendor serves the same public model.

See also: [Model mapping](./objects.md#channel-model_mapping)

## Allocation policy

<a id="allocation-tiers"></a>

### Call order

Key `allocation.tiers` · Type json · Default created from the channels' priorities when supply routing starts

Where: Allocation policy › call-order

The order channels take requests in while supplies route them, edited as the list on the Providers page. Each position is a provider (every channel of one type and address) or a single channel; positions shared by several split their requests by weight, and a provider's weight is split equally between its channels. Channels not placed come last, newest last. Models set by hand keep their own order.

Examples:

- `[[{"provider":"14:","weight":1}],[{"channel_id":7,"weight":1}]]` The official Anthropic API first; channel 7 only while it fails.
- `[[{"channel_id":3,"weight":3},{"channel_id":5,"weight":1}]]` Channels 3 and 5 share the first position: about 75% and 25% of the requests.

See also: [Supply order](./objects.md#model-allocation) · [Priority](./objects.md#supply-priority) · [Cost and priority](./gateway.md#SupplyCostOrder)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#which-supply-takes-a-request)

## User group

<a id="user_group-ratio"></a>

### Group ratio

Key `user_group.ratio` · Type ratio · Range 0– · Default 1

Where: User groups › edit

The multiplier on the catalog (official) price for users of the group: every request is charged catalog price x ratio, whatever channel serves it. The default group's ratio is the site's normal price and margin; other groups give discounts or charge more. 0 makes the group's requests free.

Examples:

- `1.12` The default group sells at 12% over the official price: a $3 / $15 per million token model costs $3.36 / $16.80.
- `1.05` A VIP discount. With a 4% payment cost it brings in $1.008 per $1, below a 3% channel fee.
- `1` Sell at the official price: every channel fee and payment cost is a loss.

See also: [Payment cost](./billing.md#PaymentCostPercent) · [Fee rate](./objects.md#channel-fee_rate)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#examples](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#examples)

<a id="user_group-api_rate"></a>

### API rate

Key `user_group.api_rate` · Type int · Unit requests / minute · Range 0– · Default 300

Where: User groups › edit

How many API requests each user of the group may send per minute, counted per user across all their keys. Requests over it get 429. Below 60 a fixed one-minute window counts them; from 60 a token bucket allows short bursts of up to 10 seconds' worth.

Examples:

- `300` Five requests a second on average per user.
- `30` The 31st request within a minute is refused until the minute is over.

<a id="user_group-public"></a>

### Public

Key `user_group.public` · Type bool · Default off

Where: User groups › edit

Whether users outside the group may pick it for their API keys, as a key's group or backup group. Off, only users in the group use it. Requests through a picked group are billed at its ratio.

See also: [Group](./objects.md#token-group) · [Backup group](./objects.md#token-backup_group) · [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio)

<a id="user_group-promotion"></a>

### Auto upgrade

Key `user_group.promotion` · Type bool · Default off

Where: User groups › edit

Moves users into this group when their total paid top-ups fall between its minimum and maximum. It is checked after each paid order; gifted credit (sign-up and invite bonuses, redemption codes, admin changes) does not count. When several groups match, the one with the highest minimum wins. A user an admin put in another group is moved too.

See also: [Minimum paid top-ups](./objects.md#user_group-min) · [Maximum paid top-ups](./objects.md#user_group-max)

<a id="user_group-min"></a>

### Minimum paid top-ups

Key `user_group.min` · Type float · Unit $ · Range 0– · Default 0

Where: User groups › edit

The total paid top-ups from which auto upgrade moves a user into the group (inclusive). Only used with auto upgrade on.

Examples:

- `100` With a maximum of 500: a user who has paid $100 up to $499.99 in total joins the group.
- `0` Every paying user matches, up to the maximum.

See also: [Auto upgrade](./objects.md#user_group-promotion) · [Maximum paid top-ups](./objects.md#user_group-max)

<a id="user_group-max"></a>

### Maximum paid top-ups

Key `user_group.max` · Type float · Unit $ · Range 0– · Default 0

Where: User groups › edit

The total paid top-ups at which the group stops matching (exclusive), so a bigger spender moves on to the next group. 0 means no upper bound. Only used with auto upgrade on.

Examples:

- `500` A user reaching $500 in total moves to the group whose range starts at 500.
- `0` The top level: users stay however much they pay.

See also: [Auto upgrade](./objects.md#user_group-promotion) · [Minimum paid top-ups](./objects.md#user_group-min)

## Routing policy

<a id="routing_policy-decision_model"></a>

### Decision model

Key `routing_policy.decision_model` · Type string

Where: Routing policies › routes

The model that reads a session's first user message and picks one of the routes. A decision model is best: it answers with a probability for every label. A small, fast chat model also works. It is charged to the caller once per session, and it cannot be another routing policy.

Examples:

- `gpt-4.1-mini` A cheap chat model that returns logprobs, so the threshold is a real probability.

See also: [Scoring](./objects.md#routing_policy-scoring) · [Confidence threshold](./objects.md#routing_policy-threshold) · [Fallback model](./objects.md#routing_policy-fallback_model)

<a id="routing_policy-scoring"></a>

### Scoring

Key `routing_policy.scoring` · Type enum · Default auto

Where: Routing policies › routes

How the decision model's confidence is measured before it is compared with the threshold. Logprobs need a non-reasoning model on a channel that returns them; Claude, reasoning models and most aggregators do not. A decision model ignores this setting.

Values:

- `auto` Auto: Logprobs where the channel returns them, else self-reported confidence for 24 hours.
- `logprobs` Logprobs only: The label's real probability; requests fall back when logprobs are missing.
- `self_reported` Self-reported only: The model answers its label and a confidence in JSON.

See also: [Confidence threshold](./objects.md#routing_policy-threshold) · [Decision model](./objects.md#routing_policy-decision_model)

<a id="routing_policy-threshold"></a>

### Confidence threshold

Key `routing_policy.threshold` · Type float · Range 0–1 · Default 0.5

Where: Routing policies › routes

The confidence the chosen route needs, from 0 to 1; below it the request goes to the fallback model. Raise it to send more borderline requests to the fallback, lower it to trust the decision model more. Self-reported confidence is only a ranking, so it compares less exactly than logprobs.

Examples:

- `0.5` A message scored 62% coding / 38% writing goes to the coding route.
- `0.8` The same message goes to the fallback, since 62% is below 80%.
- `0` The top label always wins; only a failed decision uses the fallback.

See also: [Scoring](./objects.md#routing_policy-scoring) · [Fallback model](./objects.md#routing_policy-fallback_model)

<a id="routing_policy-fallback_model"></a>

### Fallback model

Key `routing_policy.fallback_model` · Type string

Where: Routing policies › routes

Where a request goes when the confidence is below the threshold, the decision fails or the message has no text. A decision that times out counts as failed. Put your safest model here; it cannot be another routing policy.

Examples:

- `claude-sonnet-4-5` Unclear and failed decisions get a strong general model rather than a cheap one.

See also: [Confidence threshold](./objects.md#routing_policy-threshold) · [Decision model](./objects.md#routing_policy-decision_model)

<a id="routing_policy-pin_ttl_seconds"></a>

### Pin per session

Key `routing_policy.pin_ttl_seconds` · Type int · Unit s · Range 0–604800 · Default 3600

Where: Routing policies › settings

How long a session keeps the model chosen at its first message. Later turns skip the decision, keep the upstream prompt cache warm and never switch models mid-conversation. 0 classifies every request; at most 7 days.

Examples:

- `3600` A conversation stays on its model for an hour after its first message, then is classified again.
- `0` Every request pays for a decision and may land on another model.

See also: [Decision model](./objects.md#routing_policy-decision_model)

## Organization

<a id="organization-max_members"></a>

### Member limit

Key `organization.max_members` · Type int · Range 0– · Default the site default

Where: Organizations › members

The most members the organization may have, set by platform admins. It only stops new members from joining; existing members are not removed. Follow the site default, unlimited (0) or a number.

Examples:

- `20` An organization with 20 members cannot invite or add a 21st until one leaves.
- `0` No limit, whatever the site default says.

See also: [Default member limit](./orgpolicy.md#OrganizationDefaultMaxMembers)

<a id="organization-approved_models"></a>

### Approved models

Key `organization.approved_models` · Type list · Default empty (every model)

Where: Organizations › models

The most the organization may use, set by platform admins: every list of the organization stays inside it. Its default, members' lists and keys are all checked against the model actually called. A name ending in * allows a prefix, so new releases of a family follow; exact names need approving one by one. Empty means no limit.

Examples:

- `claude-*, gpt-5*` Every Claude and GPT-5 model, including ones released later; nothing else.
- `gpt-4.1-mini` Only that model; a request for any other model is refused.

See also: [Default model access](./objects.md#organization-model_whitelist) · [Model limits](./objects.md#token-model_limits)

<a id="organization-model_whitelist"></a>

### Default model access

Key `organization.model_whitelist` · Type list · Default empty (every approved model)

Where: Organizations › model-access

What members may use unless they have limits of their own, set by organization owners and admins. It is a named list or a list of models. Members with their own limits are not affected, and keys can only narrow what their creator may use. A name ending in * allows a prefix. Empty means every approved model.

Examples:

- `claude-haiku-*, gpt-4.1-mini` Members use the cheap models only; a member given their own list can use more.

See also: [Approved models](./objects.md#organization-approved_models) · [Model limits](./objects.md#token-model_limits)

<a id="organization-budget"></a>

### Organization budget

Key `organization.budget` · Type float · Unit $ · Range 0– · Default none

Where: Organizations › budget

The most all members together may spend per day, week or month; then the organization's requests are refused. They are refused until the next period starts. Each member's own budget still applies. Periods start at midnight in the platform's reset time zone; changing the period restarts the count. None means no organization-wide cap.

Examples:

- `1000 monthly` When members have spent $1,000 in the month, every request of the organization is refused until the 1st.
- `50 daily` A runaway script stops the team at $50 a day.

See also: [Member budget](./objects.md#organization-member_budget) · [Reset time zone](./billing.md#QuotaResetTimezone) · [Week starts on](./billing.md#QuotaResetWeekStart)

<a id="organization-member_budget"></a>

### Member budget

Key `organization.member_budget` · Type float · Unit $ · Range 0– · Default none

Where: Organizations › members

The most one member may spend per day, week or month in the organization, set on the member's limits. Once used up, that member's requests are refused until the next period, while the organization budget caps everyone together. Keys the organization owns have no member budget. None means no cap of the member's own.

Examples:

- `100 weekly` The member can spend $100 from Monday (or Sunday, per the site's week start) to the next week start.

See also: [Organization budget](./objects.md#organization-budget) · [Reset time zone](./billing.md#QuotaResetTimezone) · [Week starts on](./billing.md#QuotaResetWeekStart)

<a id="organization-log_io_policy"></a>

### Request and response retention

Key `organization.log_io_policy` · Type enum · Default off

Where: Organizations › general

Which of the organization's API keys keep the bodies of their requests and responses. Only owners and admins set it, here: a key's creator cannot. Stored bodies never include API keys or auth headers, are deleted after 30 days, and only owners and platform admins can read them. Members are told on their keys who turned retention on and when. Shown only while the site allows retention.

Values:

- `off` Keep for no key: No organization key keeps its request and response bodies.
- `on` Keep for every key: Every organization key keeps its bodies, new keys included.
- `selected` Keep for selected keys: Only the keys ticked in the list below keep their bodies; new keys start unticked.

Examples:

- `off` Zero data retention for the whole organization.
- `selected` An admin ticks the key of the app being debugged; the other keys keep nothing.

See also: [Allow keeping request bodies](./privacy.md#LogIOEnabled)

## API key

<a id="token-group"></a>

### Group

Key `token.group` · Type string · Default empty (the user's group)

Where: API keys › access

The user group the key's requests run in: only channels of that group serve them, billed at its ratio. It must be the user's own group or a public one. Empty uses the user's group.

Examples:

- `vip` Requests use the vip channels and pay the vip ratio, even if the user is in default.

See also: [Backup group](./objects.md#token-backup_group) · [Public](./objects.md#user_group-public) · [Groups](./objects.md#channel-group)

<a id="token-backup_group"></a>

### Backup group

Key `token.backup_group` · Type string

Where: API keys › access

A second group tried when the key's group has no channel that can take the request. A request served there is billed at the backup group's ratio and marked in the logs. With a group or backup group set, the user's own group is not tried.

Examples:

- `default` Group vip with backup default: if every vip channel for the model fails, the request runs in default at its ratio.

See also: [Group](./objects.md#token-group) · [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio)

<a id="token-model_limits"></a>

### Model limits

Key `token.model_limits` · Type list

Where: API keys › access

The models the key may call; others are refused. A name ending in * allows a prefix. With the switch on and no model selected, the key is not restricted. On an organization key it can only narrow what its creator may use, and may be a named list.

Examples:

- `gpt-4.1-mini, claude-haiku-*` A key for a chatbot that can only reach the two cheap model families.

See also: [Default model access](./objects.md#organization-model_whitelist) · [Approved models](./objects.md#organization-approved_models)

<a id="token-quota"></a>

### Spending limit

Key `token.quota` · Type float · Unit $ · Range 0– · Default empty (no limit)

Where: API keys › basics

The most the key may spend; once used up, its requests are refused. With a reset period it is the limit per period instead. It only caps the key: the account balance always applies. Empty means no limit of the key's own.

Examples:

- `10` Without a period, the key stops for good after $10 of usage.
- `5 daily` The key can spend $5 a day; the count starts over at midnight.

See also: [Reset period](./objects.md#token-quota_reset)

<a id="token-quota_reset"></a>

### Reset period

Key `token.quota_reset` · Type enum

Where: API keys › basics

How often the key's spending limit starts over. Without a period the limit is spent once. Periods start at midnight in the platform's reset time zone, weeks on its week start; changing the period restarts the count. A period needs a limit above 0.

Values:

- `daily` Daily: Starts over at midnight.
- `weekly` Weekly: Starts over at midnight on the first day of the week.
- `monthly` Monthly: Starts over at midnight on the 1st.

See also: [Spending limit](./objects.md#token-quota) · [Reset time zone](./billing.md#QuotaResetTimezone) · [Week starts on](./billing.md#QuotaResetWeekStart)
